messages.subject: initial values definition for a multistate CR model
parts:
Hi all,
I am trying to apply a multistate capture-recapture model to an experiment where we have flour bugs fed with different mixtures of flour, polypropylene + flour, polystyrene + flour, biodegradable plastic + flour, and a control group with only flour (4 treatments). Capture probability is 1 as they are in jars.
The bugs have been checked daily for 160 days (160 events) and recorded the developing stage (J for larva, P for pupa, A for adult) or if they were dead. I am working on a sample of 50 individuals (of a total of 3600 individuals) without adding the covariates for the moment in order to estimate the survival of every developing stage and the probability of transitioning from one to the other (J to P and P to A). I use the developing stage as a state so I am using a multistate model without covariates for now, with the intention to add treatment and sex as covariates once I get a good base model.

 I think I applied what I learned in "Bayesian capture-recapture inference with hidden Markov models" course  by Olivier Gimenez and colleagues, but I still get a couple of warning messages I can't solve:
- Infinite values were detected in model variable: logProb_z.
- warning: problem initializing stochastic node z[23, 157]: logProb is -Inf. (I get this one repeated for every observation of dead individuals, almost)

here my script:

# -------------------------------------------------
  # Parameters:
  # phiJ: survival probability J
  # phiP: survival probability P
  # phiA: survival probability A
  # psiJP : transition probability from J to P
  # psiPA : transition probability from P to A
  # pJ: recapture probability as J
  # pP: recapture probability as P
  # pA: recapture probability as A
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # States (z):
  # 1 alive as J
  # 2 alive as P
  # 3 alive as A
  # 4 dead
  # Observations (y):  
  # 1 not seen
  # 2 seen as J
  # 3 seen as P
  # 4 seen as A
  # -------------------------------------------------
 
  # Priors
  phiJ ~ dunif(0, 1)
  phiP ~ dunif(0, 1)
  phiA ~ dunif(0, 1)
  psiJP ~ dunif(0, 1)
  psiPA ~ dunif(0, 1)
  pJ ~ dunif(0, 1)
  pP ~ dunif(0, 1)
  pA ~ dunif(0, 1)
 
 
  # probabilities of state z(t+1) given z(t)
  gamma[1,1] <- phiJ * (1-psiJP) # alive as J not transition J to P
  gamma[1,2] <- phiJ * psiJP     # alive and transitioned to P
  gamma[1,3] <- 0                # not possible
  gamma[1,4] <- 1 - phiJ         # J dead
  gamma[2,1] <- 0                # not possible
  gamma[2,2] <- phiP * (1-psiPA) # alive as P not transition P to A
  gamma[2,3] <- phiP * psiPA     # alive and transitioned to A
  gamma[2,4] <- 1 - phiP         # P dead
  gamma[3,1] <- 0                # not possible
  gamma[3,2] <- 0                # not possible
  gamma[3,3] <- phiA             # alive as A
  gamma[3,4] <- 1 - phiA         # dead
  gamma[4,1] <- 0                # not possible
  gamma[4,2] <- 0                # not possible
  gamma[4,3] <- 0                # not possible
  gamma[4,4] <- 1                # dead
 
  # probabilities of y(t) given z(t)
  omega[1,1] <- 1 - pJ     # Pr(alive J t -> non-detected t)
  omega[1,2] <- pJ         # Pr(alive J t -> detected J t)
  omega[1,3] <- 0          #
  omega[1,4] <- 0          #
  omega[2,1] <- 1 - pP     # Pr(alive P t -> non-detected t)
  omega[2,2] <- 0          #
  omega[2,3] <- pP         # Pr(alive P t -> detected P t)
  omega[2,4] <- 0          #
  omega[3,1] <- 1 - pA     # Pr(alive A t -> non-detected t)
  omega[3,2] <- 0          #
  omega[3,3] <- 0          #
  omega[3,4] <- pA         # Pr(alive A t -> detected A t)
  omega[4,1] <- 1          # Pr(dead t -> non-detected t)
  omega[4,2] <- 0          # Pr(dead t -> detected A t)
  omega[4,3] <- 0          # Pr(dead t -> detected B t)
  omega[4,4] <- 0          # Pr(dead t -> detected C t)
 
  # likelihood
  for (i in 1:N){
    # latent state at first capture
    z[i,first[i]] <- y[i,first[i]] - 1
    for (t in (first[i]+1):K){
      # z(t) given z(t-1)
      z[i,t] ~ dcat(gamma[z[i,t-1],1:4])
      # y(t) given z(t)
      y[i,t] ~ dcat(omega[z[i,t],1:4])

  }

#'
#' Get data of first capture.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
get.first <- function(x) min(which(x != 0))

                                  pJ = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  pP = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  pA = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  z = zinits)}


#'
#' Parameters to monitor.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
parameters.to.save <- c("phiJ", "phiP", "phiA", "psiJP", "psiPA") #,"pJ", "pP", "pA"
parameters.to.save

#' MCMC settings.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
n.iter <- 5000
n.burnin <- 2000
n.chains <- 2

#'
#' Run nimble.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
mcmc.multiage <- nimbleMCMC(code = multiage,
                             constants = my.constants,
                             data = my.data,              
                             inits = initial.values,
                             monitors = parameters.to.save,
                             niter = n.iter,
                             nburnin = n.burnin,
                             nchains = n.chains)

#'
#' Inspect results.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MCMCsummary(mcmc.multiage, round = 2)


I am thinking my error is in the initial values definition and still can't find how to correct this:
zinits <- y
zinits[zinits == 0] <- sample(c(1,2,3), sum(zinits == 0), replace = TRUE)  ##one option is that the sum is not (zinits==0)
initial.values <- function(){list(phiJ = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  phiP = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  phiA = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  psiJP = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  psiPA = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  pJ = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  pP = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  pA = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  z = zinits)} #### or probably one or more factors of this list are incorrectly defined.

Can someone give me an advice on how to correct it?
Many thanks
Cecilia

messages.author: ea29cead5e3b8075
messages.subject: Re: initial values definition for a multistate CR model
parts:
Hey Cecilia, 

Your guess about your problem was correct, the primary issue was that your initial latent state assignments (zinits) were suggesting that certain transitions were possible (e.g., from 1 ->3) but the model defined them as impossible causing the those pesky -infinite values to pop up. 

Here is my suggestion that will at least let you get in the gears moving. I don't believe I changed anything else except for the following lines of code.

# Fill in the known states
zinits <- y

# For all missed observations, assign the latent state to be the latent state during the time period prior, which overwrites itself.
for(i in 1:nrow(y)){
  for(j in (first[i]+1):ncol(y)){
    if(y[i,j] == 0){
      zinits[i,j] <- zinits[i,j-1]
    }
  }
}

# Lastly, given that these appear to be daily observations, you may want to limit the initial values for the other parameters to be on the high end. You may run into issues in model runs if the initial draw for survival is really low. Here I just set them to be constant values, but you don't have to do this. 
initial.values <- function(){list(phiJ = 0.9,
                                  phiP = 0.9,
                                  phiA = 0.9,
                                  psiJP = .5,
                                  psiPA = .5,
                                  pJ = .95,
                                  pP = .95,
                                  pA = .95,
                                  z = zinits)}

Hope this helps, 

-Dan
